conflicts.quote_a: Critical** — untrusted code or fully attacker-reachable parsing with no effective boundary, or a boundary trivially bypassed by present config (`--privileged`, docker.sock mounted, secrets/metadata reachable from inside, language-jail-only sandbox, agent with full lethal trifecta and no gating).
conflicts.quote_b: Critical | Remotely exploitable now, by an unauthenticated or low-priv actor, leading to full compromise of a key asset (RCE, auth bypass, mass data exfil). Fix before anything else ships.
conflicts.why: Rating the same MCP finding (e.g. a tool with excessive agency/lethal-trifecta exposure reachable only by an authenticated caller) as Critical under A's criteria while B's criteria would bar the Critical label unless an unauthenticated or low-priv actor can reach it means the two mandatory severity conventions assign different, incompatible labels to the identical finding.

conflicts.quote_a:
Where: <file:line | resource | runtime evidence>
Threat class: <untrusted code | untrusted input | multi-tenant | agent>
Gap: <which rule (file §rule) is violated and how>
Impact: <what the attacker holds when this is exploited>
Fix: <concrete change — config snippet or pattern reference>
conflicts.quote_b:
Location: path/to/file.py:123 (and IaC/config refs)
Threat: <actor> can <action> via <vector> because <missing/weak control>,
        impacting <asset> (<C/I/A/privacy impact>).
Evidence: code excerpt or config line proving the gap.
Recommendation: specific control + where it goes; map to requirement ID.
Residual risk if accepted: one sentence.
conflicts.why: Both files declare their own field set as the mandatory, exception-free structure for every finding in the audit, so writing findings that strictly satisfy A's schema (Where/Threat class/Gap/Impact/Fix, no Evidence/Recommendation/Residual-risk fields required) does not satisfy B's binding schema (Location/Threat/Evidence/Recommendation/Residual risk), and vice versa.

conflicts.why: Rating a missing/ineffective namespace default-deny NetworkPolicy as Medium (per sota-kubernetes' severity table) while the same finding must be rated High (per sota-network-security's severity table) means an auditor cannot assign a severity that satisfies both skills' explicit severity conventions for this exact finding.

conflicts.quote_a: **Spread the rest**: forward `...rest` to the underlying DOM node, merge (don't clobber) `className`/style, and forward `ref`. A component that swallows `data-testid`, `aria-*`, or event handlers is broken.
conflicts.quote_b: **Spreading unknown props** (`<div {...userControlledObject}>`) can inject `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` or event handlers — never spread attacker-influenced objects onto DOM elements.
conflicts.why: Unconditionally forwarding all rest props onto the underlying DOM node (as the component-API rule requires, with no security carve-out) would violate the security rule against ever spreading attacker-influenced/user-controlled objects onto DOM elements.

conflicts.quote_a: **Spread the rest**: forward `...rest` to the underlying DOM node, merge (don't clobber) `className`/`style`, and forward `ref`. A component that swallows `data-testid`, `aria-*`, or event handlers is broken.
conflicts.quote_b: **Spreading unknown props** (`<div {...userControlledObject}>`) can inject `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` or event handlers — never spread attacker-influenced objects onto DOM elements.
conflicts.why: Unconditionally forwarding all rest props onto the underlying DOM node (as the component-API rule requires) is exactly the pattern the security rule forbids when any of those props originate from user/server data crossing the boundary, so a component built to the letter of one rule violates the other whenever props include untrusted data.

conflicts.quote_a:
[SEVERITY] <domain>: <one-line problem>
  Where: <file:line or component/page>
  Rule: <rules/NN §section> (+ WCAG SC number if a11y)
  Impact: <who is affected and how>
  Fix: <concrete change, ideally token/pattern-level>
  Effort: trivial | small | medium | large
conflicts.quote_b: file:line | rule violated (rules/NN §S) | severity | effort | fix
conflicts.why: Both skills mandate a specific, different required output template for reporting audit findings on the same combined review, so a single finding list cannot be formatted to satisfy both prescribed 'Finding format' structures simultaneously.

conflicts.quote_a: Any authz-sensitive or per-user/per-tenant response cached in a shared layer (Redis, CDN, shared in-process map) must carry the user/tenant — and role/scope where the value varies by it — in the cache key.
conflicts.quote_b: Personalized (auth/cookie-dependent) responses must be `Cache-Control: private` (browser only) or uncached — never `public`/`s-maxage` at a shared CDN.
conflicts.why: Following A would permit caching a personalized/authz-sensitive Server Action or SSR response at a shared CDN as long as the cache key includes the user/tenant identity, while B categorically forbids caching any personalized response at a shared CDN regardless of key design.

conflicts.quote_a: An optional dependency backing a security control is not optional. Import it unconditionally, or make the missing case a startup error.
conflicts.quote_b: run the rest, **SKIP that check with a named note** — `SKIPPED: python3 not found (CI enforces this check)` — and make the skip visible in the summary
conflicts.why: For deploy-attest.sh's ledger-verification step, if the tool needed to compute/verify the attestation hash/signature (e.g. sha256sum/openssl/gpg) is missing, Skill A requires treating that as a hard startup error (since it backs a security control), while Skill B classifies it as 'one check inside a larger run' that should be skipped-with-a-note while the rest of the script (and release) proceeds — the two cannot both be followed for the same missing dependency.
